answer: To resist sybil attacks in an AI-agent economy, require each new identity to post a bond equal to the square of current agents in its local nebula of recent joiners; the bond unlocks only after the agent wanders a unique path of sequential peer challenges whose solutions depend on the prior sparrow-timestamped state shared by the network. An attacker spawning many clones thus faces super-linear costs that cannot be parallelized, as each additional identity inflates the required stake and must wait for the shared state to advance.
